evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'I just need to ask you some questions about this might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time, okay?' — time frame given, promise of quote not explicitly stated, no clear wait for yes before moving into agenda question.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'do you have, aside from the pricing, do you have any other imported concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' Bridget then lists: packing, bed disassembly, and safe concerns. Asked before probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Joanna acknowledged packing concern ('no worries. So let me go ahead and discuss that for further with you') but never circled back to ask 'tell me more' on safe weight/logistics or bed disassembly specifics. Only surface acknowledgment, no real second-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Joanna said 'Okay, got it thank you so much' but never reflected back 'So what I'm hearing is packing, bed disassembly, and a 250-300 pound safe. Did I get that?' — moved straight into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically a two bedroom apartment usually takes three and a half to five and a half hours to complete. In your case...usually takes more time...So right now, just estimating your move more than the five to six hour mark, which is an estimated budget of 1248 dollars' — range + personalization to ground-to-ground and safe weight present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna: 'we charge by the hour...all inclusive rates. I can guarantee you there are no other fees outside of this...all the wrap to protect your furniture...taxes, insurance, credit card fees, transportation fee. Well basically everything's already in that price...two and a half hour minimum. But once we go over the minimum we only charge in fifteen minute intervals.' Full fee transparency and commitment framing delivered.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Joanna moved directly from estimate explanation into 'Now, typically a two bedroom apartment...' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or similar, and no pause before Section 6 approach.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'on time guarantee if we run late to the time to the time that we schedule we provide discounts for your move' — discount terms stated plainly, full delivery.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages' — amount and coverage type stated, but no explicit framing of 'no deductible, no fine print' or 'built into the rate, not an add-on.' Partial.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Joanna mentioned the Two Promises features mid-pricing explanation but never came back to ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closing question on the original concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Joanna: 'Okay, I think that gives me all the information that I needed. Sure.' This is throwaway language, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' — it's a reflexive empty question that invites automatic closure.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'So that being said would you like her help for this move on the twenty sixth?' is a direct ask, but immediately followed by built-in soft out: 'No problem. I'll send everything in the email as well so you can just respond to the email, give us a call. Whichever works for you, okay.' Rep presented email follow-up as equal alternative before securing a yes.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No framing of rate protection, rate-lock commitment, or deposit terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. Customer declined on the call ('I'm still looking around') and no details were confirmed — no date re-stated, no phone, no arrival window, no crew size confirmation, no crew names, no notes left.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (furniture inventory, safe weight, parking access, driveway slope, patio items) that directly informed a personalized estimate, and delivered full pricing framing with transparency on fees, minimums, and charge increments.
coaching_note: After presenting the estimate at $1,248, ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold actual silence for the customer to respond — don't fill it or pivot; this is the single highest-leverage moment to close before moving to concerns again, and Joanna skipped it entirely.
